entries.english:
1363, 19 February, Krumau. The brothers Peter, Jodok, Ulrich, and Johann von Rosenberg confirm the sale, made by Albert von Her to the parish priest Johann von Rosenberg and his successors, of the hereditary estate of Bukowa for thirteen score Prague groschen.

CXIV. We, Peter, Jodocus, Ulrich, and Johann, brothers von Rosenberg, wish the tenor of this document to come to the knowledge of all. Our liegeman Albert of Hor, called Her, has duly and reasonably sold his hereditary estate called Bukowa, situated beside the meadow of the parish church at Rosenberg, which he held from us as an homage fief, called in the Bohemian vernacular “leyno,” together with its cultivated and uncultivated fields, meadows, pastures, thickets, and part of the forest called Ostra, all as bounded and distinguished by fixed landmarks, to the discerning man Lord Johann, our devoted chaplain and parish priest of the parish church at Rosenberg, to that church, and to its lawful future parish priests, in perpetuity, for thirteen score Prague groschen. We confirm this sale with our certain knowledge, approval, and consent, and wish it to remain firm through us and our successors and not to be hindered by us or anyone else in any way. Our seals are attached as testimony. Given in the year of the Lord 1363 at Krumau, on the Sunday on which “Invocavit” is sung. Four small seals in red wax are described, including the seals of Peter, Jodocus, Ulrich, and Johann von Rosenberg.

CXV. 1363, 15 September, undated as to place. Brother Heinrich, abbot, and the whole convent of the monastery at Hohenfurt of the Cistercian order in the diocese of Prague openly declare to all present and future Christian faithful by these presents that the venerable priest Lord Ulrich, of blessed memory, son of the late Albert, master of the hospital in the Free City, out of special devotion, grace, and love for us, purchased and gave to us and our monastery, to hold in perpetuity, an annuity of one score Prague groschen from the village called Sacherleins near Deutsch-Reichenau, for sixteen score Prague groschen and forty ready money groschen of that currency, for the perpetual remedy of his soul. He stipulated that we and our successors must each year on the feast of Saint Francis the Confessor celebrate and observe the anniversary of the aforesaid Ulrich with a special mass for the dead, to be read for the salvation of his soul, and with the other religious services customary in our order. Each year on that day, in his memory, the convent is to be provided with a meal in the refectory costing twenty groschen from that annuity. The remaining portion of the annuity, namely forty Prague groschen, we must give each year to the brother of the aforesaid Lord Ulrich, our fellow brother Eberhard, a professed monk of our house, only until his death. After his death, the full meal and service are forever to be provided for the community at the same place and on the same day from the entire annuity of one score Prague groschen. In perpetual memory and clearer evidence of this, we have delivered these letters, strengthened by the manifest attachment of our seals, ours and that of our convent. Given and done in the year of the Lord 1363, on the octave of the Nativity of the Blessed and Glorious Virgin Mary. We, Brother Walther, abbot at Wilhering, father and visitor of the aforesaid monastery, having been earnestly asked and moved by entreaties, attach our seal to this page, with mature and sound counsel, as further confirmation and clear testimony that all the foregoing shall remain unaltered and inviolate always and everywhere. Given and done at the same place, day, and time. Two seals hang from parchment strips in green wax: the seal of Abbot Heinrich of Hohenfurt; the convent seal is missing; and the seal of Abbot Walther of Wilhering.
